method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Restraining Orders Act 1997 (WA), compilation from legislation.wa.gov.au (law 1817, mrdoc 48927, retrieved 7 September 2026), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_48927.txt; no regulations set a number used ($10 000, $1 000 and the periods are the Act's own)

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: Restraining Orders Act 1997 ss 3, 4, 5A, 6, 7 (definitions); 10D (FVRO); 11A, 12A (VRO); 34, 35A (MRO, paras (a)(i)-(iii)); 18, 20, 26, 29, 31, 39, 16(4)(d) (telephone and interim orders); 24A, 25, 38 (who may apply); 30A, 30F (police orders); 16A, 16B, 37, 50, 50A (duration, child respondents); 61, 61A, 61B(3) (breach); matters the court weighs, restraint terms, s 10E, Part 1C, Part 5, the s 62 defences, interstate and foreign orders and the machinery left out
